UPSTREAM: soc/intel/common/block/gpio: Fix the mask for gpio_pm_configure gpio_pm_configure clears out all the bits related to PM configuration in MISCCFG register and sets only the bits requested by mainboard. The mask as it is set currently results in preserving all PM bits instead of clearing them. This change updates the mask to ensure that the PM bits are cleared before setting the ones requested by mainboard. UPSTREAM: string.h: Move common string functions into .c file There's no clear reason why most of coreboot's basic string functions are static inline. These functions don't particularly benefit from inlining (at least not notably more than other functions). This patch moves them to string.c to be more consistent with our usual coding practices. Leaving the ctype functions as static inline because they actually seem small and collapsible enough that inlining seems reasonable. Also clarified the situation of strdup() and strconcat() a bit more, optimized strrchr() to be single-pass, fixed a bug with using strchr() to find '\0' and got rid of unnecessary register keywords. dev-lang/python: disable bluetooth USE flag Upstream gentoo introduced a new 'bluetooth' IUSE for installing some required bluez headers. Setting this USE flag adds bluez as a DEPEND to the python ebuild. Unfortunately, this creates a circular dependency: (dev-cpp/gtest-1.8.0-r1:0/0::portage-stable) depends on (dev-lang/python-2.7.15:2.7/2.7::chromiumos) (buildtime) (net-wireless/bluez-5.44-r186:0/0::chromiumos) (buildtime) (chromeos-base/libchrome-462023-r5:462023/462023::chromiumos) (buildtime) (dev-cpp/gtest-1.8.0-r1:0/0::portage-stable) (buildtime) However, disabling this USE flag just restores state to what it was before this USE flag was created, and since everything was already working, it should continue to work with the USE=-bluetooth. The 'bluetooth' USE flag is currently set globally in make.defaults, but we can use package.use.mask to disable for just python, and also ensure that this doesn't get overridden by later overlays (jetstream).
